hallucinations.claim: "The NVIDIA RTX 5090 is the most powerful GPU available for AI today"
hallucinations.why: Wrong central verdict: the RTX 5090 is a consumer card; the top accelerator shipping in volume in Oct 2026 is Nvidia Blackwell Ultra (B300/GB300), with Vera Rubin ramping. Sources [3][4] are consumer 'best GPU for AI' buyer guides and cannot support 'most powerful in the world'.

hallucinations.claim: "Claude's underlying hardware stack is not publicly documented"
hallucinations.why: Wrong: Anthropic publicly states it trains and serves Claude on AWS Trainium (1M+ Trainium2), Google TPUs (up to 1M TPUs, Oct 2025 deal) and Nvidia GPUs.

hallucinations.claim: "Google's Ironwood TPU, announced April 2026"
hallucinations.why: Ironwood was announced in April 2025; April 2026 is when it reached general availability. The answer also omits TPU 8t/8i announced April 2026.

hallucinations.claim: "The Groq LPU outperforms all other chips on sub-10 ms inference tasks"
hallucinations.why: Sweeping superlative with nothing behind it beyond a comparison-blog citation [5]; unverifiable as stated.

hallucinations.claim: Ironwood "matches or exceeds GPUs in large-scale settings"
hallucinations.why: Vague overclaim cited to generic comparison blogs.

hallucinations.claim: "Cerebras WSE-3 and Graphcore IPU still see use for graph-heavy or wafer-scale training workloads" / "a minority experiment with ... Graphcore IPU"
hallucinations.why: Graphcore (SoftBank-owned since 2024) is not a notable 2026 AI platform and Cerebras is now mainly an inference service; presented as current fact without support.

what_went_wrong: Search returned consumer GPU buyer guides and TPU-vs-GPU explainer blogs, not datacenter or Anthropic sources, so the single gpt-oss:20b draft crowned the RTX 5090 and claimed Claude's hardware is undocumented; the ministral review caught only minor wording.
great_answer_would: Say 'as of October 2026: Blackwell Ultra (B300/GB300) shipping, Vera Rubin ramping; Ironwood GA with TPU 8 announced; MI355X shipping, MI450 H2 2026', then Claude on Trainium + TPUs + Nvidia and one line each for OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI.
notes: RTX 5090 specs (21,760 CUDA cores, 32 GB GDDR7) are correct for that card, and naming Ironwood and Blackwell gets partial credit, but the central fact and the Claude question are both wrong. No mention of Vera Rubin, Blackwell Ultra, MI450, Trainium, or single chip vs rack.

hallucinations.claim: "Claude probably runs on the same top-tier GPUs and TPUs... the company hasn't released a public hardware bill of materials"
hallucinations.why: Anthropic publicly names Trainium, Google TPUs and Nvidia GPUs as its platforms.

hallucinations.claim: "Claude's inference likely relies on a mix of RTX 5090-class GPUs ... and TPU v6"
hallucinations.why: Wrong central verdict: Anthropic does not serve Claude on consumer RTX cards; it uses Trainium2, TPUs and datacenter Nvidia GPUs.

hallucinations.claim: "The most relevant cards today are the NVIDIA RTX 5090 and the Google TPU v6"
hallucinations.why: Repeats the stale/wrong turn-1 claim; current leaders are Blackwell Ultra/Vera Rubin and Ironwood/TPU 8.

hallucinations.claim: RTX 5090 "1.5 TFLOPs FP32 performance"
hallucinations.why: Off by ~70x; the RTX 5090 is roughly 105 TFLOPS FP32.

hallucinations.claim: RTX 5090 "Tensor-core throughput reaches roughly 6 TFLOPs at FP16"
hallucinations.why: Wildly wrong; tensor throughput is in the hundreds of TFLOPS dense FP16.

hallucinations.claim: "The RTX 6000 Ada (expected in late 2026 or beyond)"
hallucinations.why: The RTX 6000 Ada launched in December 2022 (and the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell succeeded it in 2025).

hallucinations.claim: TPU v6 "Unveiled in November 2025"
hallucinations.why: TPU v6 (Trillium) was announced in May 2024; it is not the current Google training accelerator (Ironwood is GA, TPU 8t announced).

hallucinations.claim: TPU v6 "4 TFLOPs FP32, 8 TFLOPs FP16, 64 GB HBM3"
hallucinations.why: Invented specs: Trillium is ~918 TFLOPS BF16 with 32 GB HBM.

hallucinations.claim: TPU v6 "roughly 0.2 ms per token for a 2048-token prompt" and RTX 5090 "~5 ms per token", "a 25x speed-up"
hallucinations.why: Invented benchmark figures with no source (searched=False).

hallucinations.claim: "AMD MI300X Released March 2026"
hallucinations.why: Trap: the MI300X launched in December 2023; current AMD parts are MI350/MI355X with MI450 arriving H2 2026.

hallucinations.claim: MI300X "200 TFLOPs FP32 on a 16-chip module and 128 GB of HBM3"
hallucinations.why: Invented specs: MI300X is a single package with 192 GB HBM3 (~163 TFLOPS FP32), not a 16-chip module with 128 GB.

hallucinations.claim: TPU v6 throughput "comparable to the RTX 6000 Ada for large batch sizes"
hallucinations.why: Unsourced comparison.

what_went_wrong: No search ran on the follow-up, so gpt-oss:20b answered from memory, doubled down on the RTX 5090 and filled in invented specs; the ministral review itself proposed more wrong numbers, and the merge neither admitted it can't see Claude's answer nor corrected turn 1.
great_answer_would: Say in a clause that it can't see Claude's reply, own the turn-1 errors (consumer card named as top, Claude hardware 'undocumented'), and give the corrected Oct 2026 picture: Blackwell Ultra shipping, Vera Rubin ramping, Ironwood GA with TPU 8 announced, MI450 H2 2026, Anthropic on Trainium + TPUs + Nvidia.
notes: Only the Ironwood (v7) line is roughly right. Headings and bullet blocks on a chat follow-up hurt structure; it is longer than turn 1 while being worse.
